questions.scenario: A company must move 80 TB from an on-premises NFS share to EFS, preserve metadata, run incremental copies before cutover, and verify transferred data. Which service is the direct fit?
questions.explanation: DataSync is designed for managed online transfers between file and object storage locations with scheduling and verification. Learn more in [What is AWS DataSync](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/what-is-datasync.html).

questions.scenario: A PostgreSQL database must move to RDS with a short cutover window. The team needs an initial load followed by ongoing change replication. Which service fits?

options.text: Amazon EBS snapshots copied by hand.

questions.explanation: AWS DMS supports full load plus change data capture for supported source and target engines. Learn more in the [AWS DMS User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/Welcome.html).

questions.scenario: External partners must keep using SFTP while files land in S3 under controlled identities and paths. Which managed service matches the protocol boundary?
questions.explanation: AWS Transfer Family provides managed SFTP and related protocol endpoints backed by S3 or EFS. Learn more in [AWS Transfer Family](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transfer/latest/userguide/what-is-aws-transfer-family.html).

questions.scenario: A remote site has petabytes of data and insufficient network bandwidth for the migration deadline. Which family of options should be evaluated?

options.text: AWS Snow Family offline transfer devices.

questions.explanation: Snow Family devices address migrations where online transfer bandwidth or duration is impractical. Learn more in [AWS Snowball Edge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/snowball/latest/developer-guide/whatisedge.html).

questions.scenario: A migration has passed its first copy test and is moving toward a production cutover. Which controls belong in the final migration plan?

options.text: Define source freeze or change-capture behavior.
Delete the source before consumers validate the target.
Validate counts, checksums, or application-level invariants.
Skip reconciliation because a managed transfer reported success.
Plan cutover, rollback, and ownership of the final sync.

questions.explanation: A safe migration controls data change, validates correctness, and makes cutover and rollback explicit. Learn more in [AWS DataSync](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/what-is-datasync.html) and [AWS DMS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/Welcome.html).
